hens_rule_text: up to 6 hens with a Tier One Backyard Chicken Keeping Permit; 7 to 15 hens need a Tier Two permit with a neighbor petition; 16 or more, and any roosters, are never allowed
permit_notes: A Backyard Chicken Keeping Permit is required under St. Paul Legislative Code Sec. 198. Tier One (1 to 6 hens) costs $26 to start plus a $16 annual renewal and needs written notice to adjacent neighbors; Tier Two (7 to 15 hens) needs a neighbor petition. Animal Control inspects yearly.
setback_notes: Coop must be at least 5 ft from property lines and at least 20 ft from neighboring residences.
coop_rules: Coop over 200 sq ft or with electricity needs a separate building or electrical permit; site plan required with the application.
zoning_notes: Citywide permit system under Legislative Code Title XX (Animals), Sec. 198, administered by the Department of Safety and Inspections, Animal Control.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.
